And don’t forget to subscribe to my newsletter and follow me on X (Twitter), LinkedIn, and YouTube for more on the future trends in business and technology.

title: Council Post: Five Practical Applications Of AI In Automation
text:
Jakob Freund is the CEO of Camunda, a software company innovating end-to-end process orchestration.
Both AI and automation are changing the nature of work. When used together, these two technologies hold great promise to improve human productivity and make existing business processes more efficient. While much of the recent media focus has been on generative AI applications like ChatGPT, there are many other practical uses of AI in automation that can both improve internal productivity and drive better customer experiences.
These technologies can be grouped into three overall areas of impact: generative, predictive and augmented intelligence.
• Generative: In this context, generative AI algorithms can be used to create new content or generate code in response to training datasets.
• Predictive: Teams can use predictive AI algorithms to make decisions or improve processes based on previous outcomes.
• Augmented Intelligence: This AI technology has the capacity to accelerate decision-making processes that typically require human intervention.
Let’s take a look at five practical applications of AI that fall within these three categories and how they can improve enterprise automation outcomes.
1. Continuously Improving Processes
It is possible to improve end-to-end processes by combining process orchestration with AI. For example, a process orchestration system gathers data on process execution and performance across a variety of endpoints (e.g., the people, systems and devices that make up a process). This process execution data can be fed into a predictive AI model to make predictions about how certain processes will perform (e.g., process duration), based on the performance of similar processes in the past.
The holy grail of self-healing processes isn’t far away with the addition of emerging augmented intelligence models. This technology has the potential to detect bottlenecks in processes, provide suggestions for enhancement and either automatically update models or update them following human validation of the decision.
2. Generating Process Testing Data
One compelling use of generative AI involves the generation of testing data for processes. For example, there are many ways that forms can produce errors, based on typical human errors—think about the myriad ways of representing dates (1.15.23 versus 15.1.23 versus January 15, 2023, etc.).
Using past human behavior as a reference, the system can create tests that have the potential to "challenge" a form, including scenarios like inputting incorrect numeric values, surpassing character limits and so on.
3. Accelerating Decision-Making
Many organizations already use automation to accelerate certain decisions, such as accepting or rejecting a mortgage application based on an applicant’s credit score and perceived risk profile. Predictive AI can be used alongside decision models to accelerate certain decision-making, such as predicting instances of fraud based on previous user data in a fraud-prevention scenario.
Companies with advanced AI capabilities can harness machine learning-ready datasets from a process orchestration system, seamlessly integrating them with internal datasets to anticipate patterns and extract valuable insights for informed decision-making.
4. Streamlining Human Tasks
Generative AI can play an important role in streamlining certain human tasks. Take, for example, a community market that wants to process applications for new vendors. By incorporating the ChatGPT API into a process model, the market could automate the extraction of pertinent data from forms to produce either acceptance or rejection emails—and generate descriptions for each approved vendor to be featured on the market's website.
5. Developing Process Models
The business and enterprise software architects or developers who write code for process models could benefit from generative AI, as well. Teams can explore the use of open-source code generators like GitHub Copilot to build and code a process model, drawing inspiration from existing models established within the organization.
Rather than beginning from square one, these tools can effectively optimize limited development resources and enhance the level of automation across the entire organization.
Potential Challenges Of Applying AI In Automation
While there are many possibilities for applying AI to automating your processes, organizations should be aware of the potential risks and challenges. Some common challenges include:
• Data Preparation Overhead: Preparing data for machine learning can be time-consuming, with data scientists and engineers spending much of their effort on this task. Gartner reports that 85% of AI projects fail, and only 53% progress from prototype to production due to data-related challenges.
• Addressing Accuracy And Bias: Accuracy and bias are persistent concerns in AI. Biased training data can lead to biased results. Human supervision is essential to verify results and mitigate these issues, especially in critical automation applications like credit assessment.
• Data Security Risks: Using publicly available models can pose security risks to sensitive data such as PII and intellectual property. Organizations often develop proprietary models from internal datasets to enhance data security and protect corporate information.
While these challenges, and others, should be taken into account when considering AI implementation, they should not deter organizations from exploring AI solutions. AI, when used in conjunction with process orchestration, has the capacity to enhance automation levels, leading to improved business operations and customer experiences.
Using Orchestration As An Accelerant For AI
Today, there are many terms to explain the optimized use of AI combined with other automation technologies—ranging from intelligent automation to hyperautomation. Ultimately, process orchestration can serve as an effective jumping-off point for the effective use of AI and automation, ensuring that the various endpoints of a process and components of the hyperautomation tech and business stacks are operating in concert with one another.
The ultimate goal is an efficient, optimized end-to-end process that improves both the employee experience and customer-facing applications. That goal is well within reach as organizations accelerate along their journey with both process orchestration and AI.

title: Council Post: Four Ways The Role Of Marketing AI Prompt Engineers Can Improve Copy
text:
Chris d’Eon, Deon Direct, is a marketing educator and consultant. He teaches at Birdrock Training. Co-author of “Leads Good, Sales Better.
In the world of marketing, AI once promised a revolution, offering the potential to generate content at incredible speed and reduced costs. However, the initial excitement faded as the AI-generated content often lacked the human touch and emotional connection required to engage readers and drive conversions.
But a new dawn is upon us where AI is shifting from a mere time-saving tool to a strategic asset in crafting content that not only resonates but also converts.
The Evolution Of AI In Marketing Copywriting
We've all encountered AI-generated content that felt mechanical and detached. For many, the initial aim was to create more content while cutting costs, and indeed, that was achieved. Yet the missing link was the content's ability to inspire action.
The role of marketing prompt engineers (yes, this is a new profession) is an emerging field that seeks to harmonize the intricacies of language with the analytical prowess of AI. The responsibility of their role is clear: to construct sophisticated instructions that guide AI to create content that aligns with brand identity and, importantly, drives sales.
Four Areas Of Improvement Marketing Prompt Engineers Are Focused On
1. Distinct Personas
The default AI persona often feels like a bland, universal template. Imagine infusing it with the charisma of Malcolm Gladwell's storytelling, Warren Buffet's wisdom and David Sedaris' humor. Marketing prompt engineers make this possible by sculpting specific personas for AI. These tailored personalities create a bridge between human expression and AI capability, resulting in content that can speak the brand's language while captivating diverse audiences.
2. Enhancing Creativity Without Compromising Accuracy
Creativity can breathe life into content, yet excessive flair might distort accuracy. This dilemma of creative finesse versus factual precision is a tightrope walk. When hiring the role of prompt engineer, ensure you bring someone on the team who has mastered the art of harnessing creativity in AI-generated content. Through careful calibration, they can amplify creative elements without veering off into misinformation.
3. Conversion-Oriented Content
Prompt engineers who are well-versed in marketing psychology can steer AI toward content that drives conversions. By strategically infusing direct-response elements, they empower AI to nudge readers toward desired actions. This fusion of AI's data processing might with marketing's strategic acumen can help unlock a potent mechanism for generating content with a purpose.
4. A Comprehensive Prompt Strategy
This journey goes beyond basic prompting. Here, prompt engineers meticulously consider factors like target audience, content length, readability, creativity, format optimization and SEO intricacies. Each piece becomes a harmonious blend of strategic direction and AI's linguistic prowess, resulting in content that's not only engaging but also geared toward conversion success.
Aligning Strategy And Content Resonance
While the technicalities of engineering are crucial, the heart of effective content remains rooted in resonating with the reader. Regardless of AI's sophistication, the onus lies on marketers to devise a strategy that resonates with their audience. The fusion of a well-crafted strategy with AI-powered content engineering leads to a symphony of engagement and conversions.
Finding Prompt Engineers
So where do you find marketing prompt engineers and what are the key elements to consider when finding the ideal candidate?
Current copywriters have been spending the most time learning the new AI systems and are an excellent place to turn to for optimized marketing prompts. As some fear for their jobs, they are therefore adding AI solutions to their arsenal of talents.
SEO experts also have a unique expertise in combining words with technology, so they are good individuals to turn to. Lastly, AI software engineers who dive into the details of LLM and AI have been touting themselves as prompt engineers on Upwork and Fiverr. All are good, but the ideal candidate would typically be your current copywriter who has in-depth knowledge of your product, style, tone and more. Simply ask them about their experience with AI and prompt creation and work forward from there.
Forging The Future Of AI-Driven Marketing
As AI and human ingenuity intertwine, a new era emerges in marketing. The focus shifts from churning out content en masse to crafting meaningful narratives that inspire action. The role of prompt engineers becomes pivotal in this transformation, guiding AI to not just write but to connect, engage and convert.
While the responsibility of strategic resonance rests with marketers, the tools at our disposal have never been more potent. We stand at the crossroads of a future where AI and human intent coalesce to create content that doesn't just fill spaces but shapes decisions.

title: Council Post: AI Innovation Or Speculation: A Guide To Understanding The Difference
text:
Peter Evans is the CEO of Xtract One Technologies
Artificial intelligence (AI) is undoubtedly having a moment. Prompted by a flurry of product releases that seemed to gain instant popularity—OpenAI’s ChatGPT was briefly the fastest app to gain 100 million daily active users—leading technology companies, scrappy startups, forward-thinking entrepreneurs and, of course, investors are rushing to build the next big thing powered by AI.
According to Pitchbook, a research firm that tracks investment capital, investors have poured more than $15 billion into generative AI companies in the first half of 2023. Meanwhile, hundreds of AI startups have launched this year, reinvigorating whole cities (paywall) like San Francisco and reorienting the tech workforce at a time of deep disruption.
Naturally, some companies are AI-focused in name only. As one Axios headline quipped, “In tech, everything is labeled ‘AI’ now.” In this environment, where the hype is real and the potential endless, it can be difficult to differentiate speculation from innovation.
Innovation builds upon what came before it to bring consumers new value, products and services. In contrast, speculation is want-to-be innovation, leveraging the potential for innovation to attract attention, raise money and, almost inevitably, “change the world.”
Is It Innovation Or Speculation?
That’s why we need to define innovation for the age of AI, creating a rubric for determining the difference between a great idea and a truly ground-breaking product. Here are three criteria we can use to help evaluate the innovative potential of AI companies, products and services so we can best assess their efficacy and potential impact moving forward.
1. Real-World Implications
To understand if a product or service is truly groundbreaking, we should ask, “What are people actually doing with it?” Is it changing the way people perform work, connect with their communities or live their lives? When it comes to AI, we're seeing these implications emerging.
Although large language models (LLMs) and image generators have attracted the most attention, they're far from the only AI solutions impacting our day-to-day lives. Some prominent real-world implications include:
Security: Digital and physical security is being enhanced by AI-powered solutions that identify threats, analyze risks and empower human specialists to intervene.
Content: Although generative AI is obviously attracting a lot of attention, the technology has been influencing our social media feeds, news alerts and other information-oriented services for years.
E-Commerce: AI has changed the face of e-commerce. It's used for personalized product recommendations, automated customer support and predictive analytics for inventory management. These innovations have transformed shopping experiences, arguably making them more convenient and efficient.
Real-world use cases don’t inherently make a product or service innovative, but it’s a necessary first step to disruptive potential.
2. Prolonged Market Impact
Truly innovative products and services make a meaningful market impact. As of today, over 40% of U.S. professionals say they've used ChatGPT at work. This could suggest a genuine market impact.
However, understanding a product or service’s potential requires a protracted analysis to see if it actually lasts the test of time. For example, The Washington Post (paywall) reported that ChatGPT lost users for the first time in June 2023 as web and mobile traffic fell nearly 10% month-to-month.
The lesson here is simple: It can be difficult to determine the difference between innovation and speculation in the short term. A protracted analysis provides a more comprehensive framework for evaluating a product's or service’s efficacy.
3. Sustainable Implementation
Speculative products and services are a flash in the pan. They burn hot and quickly disappear. Often, they rely on overhyped potential or unique market forces that make them temporarily popular or highly valued.
Innovative products have a pathway to sustainable implementation, moving beyond the hype cycle and the subsequent trough of disillusionment into true and pragmatic growth, including operational efficiencies and consumer interest, which make their long-term viability more secure.
Conclusion
In this exciting AI era, identifying genuine innovation can be challenging amid the white noise of hype and speculation. Nonetheless, by applying these criteria, we can better identify ground-breaking products and services that truly have the potential to change the world.
As we move forward, it's essential to focus our energies not just on what sounds exciting but on what can sustainably transform our societies for the better. In doing so, we'll ensure that the age of AI isn't just a flash in the pan but a lasting era of real and transformative innovation.
